subject: Genetics
title: Aging as Epigenetic Drift
description: A 60-second lesson on Aging as Epigenetic Drift.

hook.text: Identical twins look alike at 5 and different at 50. Their DNA hasn't changed.

buildup.text: As we age, methylation patterns degrade. Some genes gain marks, others lose them.

discovery.text: Epigenetic drift explains why age is the biggest cancer risk factor.

twist.text: But aging isn't random degradation. Specific, predictable methylation changes occur at certain sites.

climax.text: If aging is epigenetic, it might be reversible.

punchline.text: You don't age because genes break. The marks drift.

quiz.question: What is epigenetic drift?
options: Gradual changes in methylation patterns over time
